title: introduce-presubmit-toolkit-and-incremental-dep-refresh
author: Samantha Ortiz
commits: Add incremental dep-refresh script + lightweight lockfile snapshotter
Wire toolkit into presubmit manifest and add GitHub Action wrapper
Add integration tests for presubmit cache warming and minimal network mode
Docs: presubmit runbook and troubleshooting notes
Fix: stable exit codes and retry backoff for flaky networked checks
Polish: lint and static checks, add telemetry counters
release_notes: Adds a lightweight presubmit toolkit that enables incremental dependency refresh checks and a compact presubmit manifest. This reduces presubmit setup time for common dev flows and introduces a safe, staged dep-refresh job for CI. No API changes. Backwards-compatible. Rollout: enabled for core repo presubmit lanes then opt-in for language-specific lanes.
description: Context and motivation: presubmit setup time and noisy dependency refreshes continue to be a major source of CI latency and developer interruption. This PR introduces a small presubmit toolkit (Go binary + GitHub Action wrapper + helper scripts) that lets us run targeted, incremental dependency refresh checks and anchors a compact presubmit manifest to reduce per-PR init work. The goal is predictable, fast feedback for common change patterns while keeping a path to full refresh jobs for periodic hygiene. Changes summary: 1) tools/presubmit-toolkit: Go-based CLI that computes a minimal dependency surface, snapshots relevant lockfile fragments, and optionally runs a shallow network lookup (cached) to validate transitive availability. 2) ci/actions/presubmit-toolkit/action.yml: lightweight Action wrapper to run the toolkit in GitHub environments with bounded network and cache options. 3) ci/scripts/incremental-dep-refresh.sh: bash shim used by traditional CI lanes for back-compat. 4) ci/presubmit/manifest.yaml: new compact presubmit manifest describing fast lanes (lint, unit, dep-incremental) and slow lanes (integration/longtests) to be scheduled separately. 5) .github/workflows/presubmit-toolkit.yml: new workflow that exercises cache-warm fast lanes and emits telemetry. 6) docs/ci/presubmit.md: runbook with troubleshooting and opt-in instructions. Testing and verification: - Local unit tests for toolkit functions and integration test that runs in a hermetic docker image (tools/presubmit-toolkit/tests/integration_test.go). - Verified on a staging org repo with representative dependency graphs; measured median presubmit init time drop from ~45s to ~18s for fast lanes. - CI matrix: passed linux/amd64 and linux/arm64, lint and go vet green. Rollout plan: 1) Merge to main with canary enabled for core fast lanes for 24h (done in staging). 2) Monitor presubmit latency metrics (ci.presubmit.init_time_p50/p95) and failure rates (ci.presubmit.dep_incr_failures). 3) Gradually opt-in additional repos and language lanes; fallback flag available to disable the incremental dep-check per-repo. Observability and telemetry: toolkit increments counters for cache_hit, cache_miss, network_probe_count, and emits fingerprint hashes of lock fragments (non-sensitive). We added Grafana panels and an alert for sustained dep_incr_fail_rate > 2% over 30m. Backward compatibility and safety: - The incremental dep-refresh is opt-in by default for language lanes; the full refresh job still runs nightly. - Tool exits with non-zero only on deterministic validation failures; transient network failures are retried with exponential backoff and treated as warnings in early rollout. Security and compliance: the toolkit does not transmit repository secrets; network probes are limited to package registry hostnames and executed under a short-lived action token. Implementation notes and trade-offs: - Chose Go for a small, portable binary to keep the runtime hermetic across runners. - We intentionally keep the dependency surface minimal and avoid embedding registry clients; the network probe uses HEAD requests to registry endpoints and validates signatures where available. - The approach favors lower latency and deterministic failure modes over exhaustive resolution — full refresh coverage remains in scheduled hygiene jobs. Checklist: - [x] Unit tests added - [x] Integration test added - [x] Documentation updated - [x] Telemetry and dashboards wired - [x] Rollout plan and feature flag in manifest - [x] Security review (lightweight) Known limitations and follow-ups: - Need a cross-language shim for package managers we don't yet support (Ruby/Python minimal support exists; Node/PyPI improvements planned). Tracked as ENG-1889. - Candidate improvement: add optional delta-only caching for large monorepo paths to further reduce init time (follow-up PR). Related work: builds on previous presubmit decomposition efforts (ENG-1733) and the CI-fastpath discussions in linear (ENG-1824). Linear and support links: ENG-1824, ENG-1831; support ticket SUP-627.
